relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED from the arXiv title page (arXiv:2411.03801v2, math.GT): two-author, subject and identifier match the seeded entry. Citation sites: computations/probes/borromean_nz_adjoint_torsion.py:82 and computations/probes/borromean_jones_1loop_torsion.py:50, both asserting that the 1-loop conjecture used below is now a THEOREM for both calibration cases because 4_1 is 2-bridge. LOAD-BEARING AND CORRECT: the PDF's Theorem 1.1 reads verbatim 'The 1-loop equals torsion conjecture holds for hyperbolic 2-bridge knots', and the introduction confirms the object is the 1-loop power series attached to an ideal triangulation of a cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold, whose constant term is conjectured to equal the adjoint Reidemeister torsion. 4_1 is a hyperbolic 2-bridge knot, so the probes' hypothesis check is sound; the reference entry's separate claim that 6_2 is 2-bridge with fraction 11/3 is also correct. Note the probes route the OTHER calibration case (Borromean rings) to pandey-wong-2023 rather than stretching this theorem past its hypothesis - the boundary is respected, which is what a citation at this strength requires.

keyResults.statement: The 1-loop equals adjoint-Reidemeister-torsion conjecture holds for hyperbolic 2-bridge knots.
keyResults.useForFolio: Upgrades the 4_1 reading of exp(2 c_0) = 1/|det J_NZ| from conjecture-conditional to theorem-backed in the Borromean 1-loop/torsion probes.

keyResults.statement: Both invariants are determinants over the trace field - the 1-loop from Neumann-Zagier matrices/shapes (equivalently the Ptolemy Jacobian), the torsion from Fox calculus on a pi_1 presentation in the adjoint representation - and the proof reconciles the two via the already-registered [ohtsuki-takata2015] result plus an explicit computation.
keyResults.useForFolio: Names precisely which determinant the corpus's det J_NZ computation is, and why the identification is not definitional.

proposedActions.rationale: Cited in two probes for exactly what Theorem 1.1 states, with the hypothesis (2-bridge) checked and the out-of-scope case routed to a different source. Nothing to correct.
